affectedPublicSurfaces: demo.app-juli.com — the public target is resolved through an upstream definition the deployment owns, and cutover becomes an atomic replacement plus a graceful reload

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: the candidate remains loopback-only and is verified before any traffic moves, exactly as #838 established; this slice changes only how traffic is repointed once verification has already passed

journeys.name: graceful-cutover-drops-nothing
journeys.entryUrl: https://demo.app-juli.com/ under continuous load during a release
assertions: requests in flight during cutover complete rather than erroring
no request observes an unavailable upstream at any point in the release
the upstream definition is replaced atomically, then reloaded gracefully — never edited in place while serving

journeys.name: invalid-configuration-is-rejected-without-interrupting-service
journeys.entryUrl: the web server configuration test, run before every reload
assertions: an invalid configuration is rejected before any reload is attempted
the previously loaded configuration keeps serving, unchanged
the deploy exits non-zero and the live site is unaffected

journeys.name: the-live-definition-is-the-single-source-of-truth
journeys.entryUrl: the owned upstream definition on the server
assertions: what is serving can be read from the live upstream definition alone
the immediately previous definition is retained beside it as the undo
site configuration is otherwise unchanged apart from the indirection

migrationCompatibility.notes: The slice changes how traffic is repointed. It touches no database, queue, or persistence surface. The #834 gate still runs before any candidate starts, unchanged from #838.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: restore the retained previous upstream definition and reload; this slice makes that undo *possible* and manual, and #840 makes it automatic on a post-cutover check failure

doNotInfer: post-cutover checks or automatic rollback — that is #840
paired slots for the API or landing — that is #843
a combined deploy command or release record — that is #844
percentage-based traffic canaries or request mirroring — explicitly out of scope in PRD #820
new DNS records, subdomains, or TLS certificates
changing what the candidate verification in #838 asserts
